merger_name: Australian Venue Co – assets of The Breakwater, Hillarys and Print Hall, Perth

anzsic_codes.name: Amusement and Other Recreational Activities n.e.c.

merger_description:
AVC Operations Pty Ltd (**AVC**) proposes to acquire substantially all of the assets of the licensed venues trading as The Breakwater and Print Hall (including the exclusive right to carry on the business in succession of the vendor and the benefit of the existing lease) from Wintime Nominees Pty Ltd and Sunliner Holdings Pty Ltd respectively (the **Acquisition**). The business assets of The Breakwater and Print Hall are currently owned and operated by each respective vendor as part of Night Owl Group.

AVC is a subsidiary of Australian Venue Co. Holdings Limited which operates over 200 licensed venues throughout Australia and New Zealand, primarily pubs, as well as some bars, clubs and licensed restaurants. Its venues are individually branded and are mostly located in inner-city and metropolitan areas, offering a range of products and services including food, alcoholic and non-alcoholic beverages, function rooms, live entertainment and gaming facilities.

The Breakwater is a licensed venue located at 203/58 Southside Drive, Hillarys WA 6025. The venue is a waterfront destination featuring multiple bars, a restaurant, entertainment facilities (i.e. bowling and shuffleboard) and function rooms.

Print Hall is a multi-level licensed venue located at Brookfield Place, 125 St Georges Terrace, Perth WA 6000. The venue is a heritage-listed entertainment precinct featuring multiple bars, a cellar wine bar, restaurants and a rooftop terrace.

AVC will commence hospitality operations from each venue by taking on the existing leases following completion of the Acquisition.

events.title: Notification waiver determination published

determination_table_content.details:
In making this notification waiver determination, the Australian
Competition and Consumer Commission (ACCC) has considered
information provided by the applicant and had regard to the factors
in section 51ABV(2)(b) of the Act.
Based on the information provided in the application, including the
parties’ revenue in Australia, the ACCC considers that, if the
Acquisition were put into effect, the notification thresholds would be
met.
The ACCC is unable to reach a view that the Acquisition would not be
likely to raise competition issues in any market based on the
information provided, given:
a. there is horizontal overlap between Australian Venue Co’s
existing venues and Print Hall and The Breakwater in the
supply of dining, function and on-premises liquor services at
pub-style venues and other retail hospitality venues in the
Perth metropolitan area
b. Australian Venue Co already owns venues in the Perth CBD
which may closely compete with Print Hall
c. the extent to which Australian Venue Co is likely to be
constrained by alternative suppliers of dining, function and
on-premises liquor services in the local areas surrounding
Perth CBD and Hillarys post-acquisition is uncertain.
The ACCC considers that these potential competition issues warrant
consideration through the notification process, including via
consultation with third parties.
Given the above, the ACCC has determined not to make the
notification waiver determination applied for.
The ACCC considers that the determination is consistent with the
object of the Act and the interests of consumers in promoting
competition.
For more information about the ACCC’s approach to considering
notification waiver applications and to assessing competition
effects more generally, see the ACCC’s guidance on notification
waivers and merger assessment guidelines.
